Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/x86/kernel/machine_kexec_64.c`**
   - In the `free_transition_pgtable` function, after freeing each page table (p4d, pud, pmd, pte), the corresponding pointer in the `image->arch` structure is set to `NULL`. This prevents potential double free errors by ensuring that the pointers do not reference freed memory.
   - The call to `free_transition_pgtable(image)` in the `init_transition_pgtable` function's error handling section has been removed. This change defers the responsibility of freeing the page tables to the `machine_kexec_cleanup()` function.

2. **File: `arch/x86/kernel/machine_kexec_32.c`**
   - Similar to the changes in the 64-bit version, the `machine_kexec_free_page_tables` function now sets each pointer (pgd, pmd0, pmd1, pte0, pte1) to `NULL` after freeing the corresponding page. 
   - The call to `machine_kexec_free_page_tables(image)` in the `machine_kexec_alloc_page_tables` function's error handling section has been removed, which also defers the cleanup responsibility to `machine_kexec_cleanup()`.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications in both files are related in that they address the same underlying issue of preventing double free errors during memory allocation failures in the kexec loading process. By removing the immediate cleanup calls in the allocation functions and ensuring that pointers are set to `NULL` after freeing, both implementations now rely on a centralized cleanup function (`machine_kexec_cleanup()`) to handle memory deallocation. This change enhances the robustness of the code by preventing potential crashes due to double freeing of memory, which was reported as a bug.

   - The call to `machine_kexec_free_page_tables(image)` was removed from the `machine_kexec_alloc_page_tables` function when memory allocation fails, preventing double freeing of the page tables.

2. **File: `arch/x86/kernel/machine_kexec_64.c`**
   - Similar to the 32-bit version, in the `free_transition_pgtable` function, after each `free_page` call, the corresponding pointer (e.g., `image->arch.p4d`, `image->arch.pud`, etc.) is set to `NULL`.
   - The call to `free_transition_pgtable(image)` was removed from the `init_transition_pgtable` function in the error handling section, which prevents double freeing of the transition page table.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications in both files are related to the handling of memory allocation failures during the kexec process. The changes ensure that when memory allocation fails, the cleanup functions (`machine_kexec_free_page_tables` and `free_transition_pgtable`) do not attempt to free already freed memory, which was causing crashes reported by syzbot. By setting the pointers to `NULL` after freeing, the code prevents future attempts to free the same memory, thus avoiding double free errors. This approach centralizes error handling in the cleanup functions, ensuring that memory management is handled more safely and effectively.

>From ff82bedd3e12f0d3353282054ae48c3bd8c72012 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Tetsuo Handa <penguin-kernel@I-love.SAKURA.ne.jp>
Date: Wed, 9 May 2018 12:12:39 +0900
Subject: [PATCH v3] x86/kexec: avoid double free_page() upon do_kexec_load() failure.

syzbot is reporting crashes after memory allocation failure inside
do_kexec_load() [1]. This is because free_transition_pgtable() is called
by both init_transition_pgtable() and machine_kexec_cleanup() when memory
allocation failed inside init_transition_pgtable().

Regarding 32bit code, machine_kexec_free_page_tables() is called by both
machine_kexec_alloc_page_tables() and machine_kexec_cleanup() when memory
allocation failed inside machine_kexec_alloc_page_tables().

Fix this by leaving the error handling to machine_kexec_cleanup()
(and optionally setting NULL after free_page()).

[1] https://syzkaller.appspot.com/bug?id=91e52396168cf2bdd572fe1e1bc0bc645c1c6b40

Fixes: f5deb79679af6eb4 ("x86: kexec: Use one page table in x86_64 machine_kexec")
Fixes: 92be3d6bdf2cb349 ("kexec/i386: allocate page table pages dynamically")
Reported-by: syzbot <syzbot+d96f60296ef613fe1d69@syzkaller.appspotmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Tetsuo Handa <penguin-kernel@I-love.SAKURA.ne.jp>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de>
Acked-by: Baoquan He <bhe@redhat.com>
Cc: thomas.lendacky@amd.com
Cc: prudo@linux.vnet.ibm.com
Cc: Huang Ying <ying.huang@intel.com>
Cc: syzkaller-bugs@googlegroups.com
Cc: takahiro.akashi@linaro.org
Cc: H. Peter Anvin <hpa@zytor.com>
Cc: akpm@linux-foundation.org
Cc: dyoung@redhat.com
Cc: kirill.shutemov@linux.intel.com
Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/201805091942.DGG12448.tMFVFSJFQOOLHO@I-love.SAKURA.ne.jp

Here is the root cause:
The bug is caused by multiple functions attempting to free the same memory pages when memory allocation fails during the kexec load process. Specifically, both `init_transition_pgtable()` and `machine_kexec_cleanup()` (in the 64-bit code) and `machine_kexec_alloc_page_tables()` and `machine_kexec_cleanup()` (in the 32-bit code) were calling free functions on the same page tables, leading to a double free scenario.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void machine_kexec_free_page_tables(struct kimage *image)
 {
 	free_page((unsigned long)image->arch.pgd);
+	image->arch.pgd = NULL;
 #ifdef CONFIG_X86_PAE
 	free_page((unsigned long)image->arch.pmd0);
+	image->arch.pmd0 = NULL;
 	free_page((unsigned long)image->arch.pmd1);
+	image->arch.pmd1 = NULL;
 #endif
 	free_page((unsigned long)image->arch.pte0);
+	image->arch.pte0 = NULL;
 	free_page((unsigned long)image->arch.pte1);
+	image->arch.pte1 = NULL;
 }
 
 #endif
 	    !image->arch.pte0 || !image->arch.pte1) {
-		machine_kexec_free_page_tables(image);
 		return -ENOMEM;
 	}
